reason: The PR changes enumeration-presolve row scoring, removes similar binary rows, and changes propagation work. These are solver search and reduction decisions, not merely local code cleanup.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Scoring rows by implication potential and suppressing overlapping rows may spend the enumeration budget on stronger reductions, changing the MIP search trajectory and total solve behavior.
workload_exposure_plan: Use binary MIP instances whose presolve enters enumeration; record reductions and full solve outcomes on the same original models for base and PR builds.
mathematical_risk: An invalid enumeration reduction or clique implication can exclude feasible integer solutions or produce an invalid bound.
independent_check_plan: Check primal solutions against original MIP models and compare proven statuses and bounds with an independent solver on tractable cases.
hidden_generalization_plan: Use paired held-out binary MIP families with fixed limits and seeds; report solved rate, time, gap trajectory, and regressions by family.
overlap_review: The PR touches presolve and clique-table files also used by later PRs; compare changed hunks and choose disjoint historical baselines before creating additional tasks from the same series.
causal_chain: Implication-based row scoring and overlap suppression redirect a bounded enumeration budget toward different reductions, which can change the downstream MIP tree and proof time.
structural_trigger: Binary MIP rows eligible for enumeration presolve, with enough candidate overlap for row suppression.
activation_probe: Count calls to enumerateSolutions, candidate and removed rows, reductions, and presolve time before scoring any hidden effect.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze binary MIP families by structural row criteria and include control families before running hidden paired comparisons.
resource_risk: Extra row scoring and overlap comparisons can increase presolve cost or memory on instances with many candidate rows.
